NKJV.1: Again, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NKJV.2: “Son of man, write down the name of the day, this very day—the king of Babylon started his siege against Jerusalem this very day.
NKJV.3: And utter a parable to the rebellious house, and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “Put on a pot, set it on, And also pour water into it.
NKJV.4: Gather pieces of meat in it, Every good piece, The thigh and the shoulder. Fill it with choice cuts;
NKJV.5: Take the choice of the flock. Also pile fuel bones under it, Make it boil well, And let the cuts simmer in it.”
NKJV.6: ‘Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: “Woe to the bloody city, To the pot whose scum is in it, And whose scum is not gone from it! Bring it out piece by piece, On which no lot has fallen.
NKJV.7: For her blood is in her midst; She set it on top of a rock;  She did not pour it on the ground, To cover it with dust.
NKJV.8: That it may raise up fury and take vengeance,  I have set her blood on top of a rock, That it may not be covered.”
NKJV.9: ‘Therefore thus says the Lord GOD:  “Woe to the bloody city! I too will make the pyre great.
NKJV.10: Heap on the wood, Kindle the fire; Cook the meat well, Mix in the spices, And let the cuts be burned up.
NKJV.11: “Then set the pot empty on the coals, That it may become hot and its bronze may burn, That its filthiness may be melted in it, That its scum may be consumed.
NKJV.12: She has grown weary with lies, And her great scum has not gone from her. Let her scum be in the fire!
NKJV.13: In your filthiness is lewdness. Because I have cleansed you, and you were not cleansed, You will not be cleansed of your filthiness anymore, Till I have caused My fury to rest upon you.
NKJV.14: I, the LORD, have spoken it; It shall come to pass, and I will do it; I will not hold back, Nor will I spare, Nor will I relent; According to your ways And according to your deeds They will judge you,” Says the Lord GOD.’ ”
NKJV.15: Also the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NKJV.16: “Son of man, behold, I take away from you the desire of your eyes with one stroke; yet you shall neither mourn nor weep, nor shall your tears run down.
NKJV.17: Sigh in silence, make no mourning for the dead; bind your turban on your head, and put your sandals on your feet; do not cover your lips, and do not eat man’s bread of sorrow.”
NKJV.18: So I spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening my wife died; and the next morning I did as I was commanded.
NKJV.19: And the people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things signify to us, that you behave so?”
NKJV.20: Then I answered them, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NKJV.21: ‘Speak to the house of Israel, “Thus says the Lord GOD: ‘Behold, I will profane My sanctuary, your arrogant boast, the desire of your eyes, the delight of your soul; and your sons and daughters whom you left behind shall fall by the sword.
NKJV.22: And you shall do as I have done; you shall not cover your lips nor eat man’s bread of sorrow.
NKJV.23: Your turbans shall be on your heads and your sandals on your feet; you shall neither mourn nor weep, but you shall pine away in your iniquities and mourn with one another.
NKJV.24: Thus Ezekiel is a sign to you; according to all that he has done you shall do; and when this comes, you shall know that I am the Lord GOD.’ ”
NKJV.25: ‘And you, son of man—will it not be in the day when I take from them their stronghold, their joy and their glory, the desire of their eyes, and that on which they set their minds, their sons and their daughters:
NKJV.26: that on that day one who escapes will come to you to let you hear it with your ears?
NKJV.27: On that day your mouth will be opened to him who has escaped; you shall speak and no longer be mute. Thus you will be a sign to them, and they shall know that I am the LORD.’ ”

ESV.1: In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
ESV.2: “Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day. The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem this very day.
ESV.3: And utter a parable to the rebellious house and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: “Set on the pot, set it on; pour in water also;
ESV.4: put in it the pieces of meat, all the good pieces, the thigh and the shoulder; fill it with choice bones.
ESV.5: Take the choicest one of the flock; pile the logs  under it; boil it well; seethe also its bones in it.
ESV.6: “Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose corrosion is in it, and whose corrosion has not gone out of it! Take out of it piece after piece, without making any choice.
ESV.7: For the blood she has shed is in her midst; she put it on the bare rock; she did not pour it out on the ground to cover it with dust.
ESV.8: To rouse my wrath, to take vengeance, I have set on the bare rock the blood she has shed, that it may not be covered.
ESV.9: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the bloody city! I also will make the pile great.
ESV.10: Heap on the logs, kindle the fire, boil the meat well, mix in the spices,  and let the bones be burned up.
ESV.11: Then set it empty upon the coals, that it may become hot, and its copper may burn, that its uncleanness may be melted in it, its corrosion consumed.
ESV.12: She has wearied herself with toil;  its abundant corrosion does not go out of it. Into the fire with its corrosion!
ESV.13: On account of your unclean lewdness, because I would have cleansed you and you were not cleansed from your uncleanness, you shall not be cleansed anymore till I have satisfied my fury upon you.
ESV.14: I am the LORD. I have spoken; it shall come to pass; I will do it. I will not go back; I will not spare; I will not relent; according to your ways and your deeds you will be judged, declares the Lord GOD.”
ESV.15: The word of the LORD came to me:
ESV.16: “Son of man, behold, I am about to take the delight of your eyes away from you at a stroke; yet you shall not mourn or weep, nor shall your tears run down.
ESV.17: Sigh, but not aloud; make no mourning for the dead. Bind on your turban, and put your shoes on your feet; do not cover your lips, nor eat the bread of men.”
ESV.18: So I spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening my wife died. And on the next morning I did as I was commanded.
ESV.19: And the people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things mean for us, that you are acting thus?”
ESV.20: Then I said to them, “The word of the LORD came to me:
ESV.21: ‘Say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your power, the delight of your eyes, and the yearning of your soul, and your sons and your daughters whom you left behind shall fall by the sword.
ESV.22: And you shall do as I have done; you shall not cover your lips, nor eat the bread of men.
ESV.23: Your turbans shall be on your heads and your shoes on your feet; you shall not mourn or weep, but you shall rot away in your iniquities and groan to one another.
ESV.24: Thus shall Ezekiel be to you a sign; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’
ESV.25: “As for you, son of man, surely on the day when I take from them their stronghold, their joy and glory, the delight of their eyes and their soul's desire, and also their sons and daughters,
ESV.26: on that day a fugitive will come to you to report to you the news.
ESV.27: On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive, and you shall speak and be no longer mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD.”

CSB17.1: The word of the LORD came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month:
CSB17.2: “Son of man, write down today’s date, this very day. The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem this very day. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.3:
Now speak a parable ⓓ to the rebellious house. Tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says: Put the pot ⓔ on the fire —
put it on,
and then pour water into it!
CSB17.4:
Place the pieces of meat in it,
every good piece —
thigh and shoulder.
Fill it with choice bones.
CSB17.5:
Take the choicest of the flock
and also pile up the fuel [1] under it.
Bring it to a boil
and cook the bones in it.
CSB17.6:
“‘Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the city of bloodshed, ⓕ
the pot that has corrosion inside it,
and its corrosion has not come out of it!
Empty it piece by piece;
lots should not be cast for its contents.
CSB17.7:
For the blood she shed [2] is still within her.
She put it out on the bare rock;
she didn’t pour it on the ground
to cover it with dust. ⓖ
CSB17.8:
In order to stir up wrath and take vengeance, ⓗ
I have put her blood on the bare rock,
so that it would not be covered.
CSB17.9:
“‘Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the city of bloodshed! ⓘ
I myself will make the pile of kindling large.
CSB17.10:
Pile on the logs and kindle the fire!
Cook the meat well
and mix in the spices! [3] [4]
Let the bones be burned!
CSB17.11:
Set the empty pot on its coals
so that it becomes hot and its copper glows.
Then its impurity will melt inside it;
its corrosion will be consumed. ⓙ
CSB17.12:
It has frustrated every effort; [5]
its thick corrosion will not come off.
Into the fire with its corrosion!
CSB17.13:
Because of the depravity of your uncleanness —
since I tried to purify you,
but you would not be purified from your uncleanness —
you will not be pure again
until I have satisfied my wrath on you. ⓚ
CSB17.14:
I, the LORD, have spoken.
It is coming, and I will do it! ⓛ
I will not refrain, I will not show pity,
and I will not relent.
I [6] will judge you

This is the declaration of the Lord GOD.’”
CSB17.15: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
CSB17.16: “Son of man, I am about to take the delight of your eyes <sup>ⓝ</sup> away from you with a fatal blow. But you must not lament or weep or let your tears flow. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.17: Groan quietly; do not observe mourning rites for the dead. <sup>ⓑ</sup> Put on your turban and strap your sandals on your feet; do not cover your mustache or eat the bread of mourners.” <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓒ</sup>

CSB17.20: So I answered them: “The word of the LORD came to me:

CSB17.22: Then you will do just as I have done: You will not cover your mustache or eat the bread of mourners.

CSB17.25: “As for you, son of man, know that on that day I will take from them their stronghold — their pride and joy, the delight of their eyes, and the longing of their hearts — as well as their sons and daughters.
CSB17.26: On that day a fugitive will come to you and report the news. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.27: On that day your mouth will be opened to talk with him; you will speak and no longer be mute. <sup>ⓘ</sup> So you will be a sign for them, and they will know that I am the LORD.”

NLT.1: On January 15, during the ninth year of King Jehoiachin’s captivity, this message came to me from the LORD:
NLT.2: “Son of man, write down today’s date, because on this very day the king of Babylon is beginning his attack against Jerusalem.
NLT.3:
Then give these rebels an illustration with this message from the Sovereign LORD: “Put a pot on the fire,
and pour in some water.
NLT.4:
Fill it with choice pieces of meat —
the rump and the shoulder
and all the most tender cuts.
NLT.5:
Use only the best sheep from the flock,
and heap fuel on the fire beneath the pot.
Bring the pot to a boil,
and cook the bones along with the meat.
NLT.6:
“Now this is what the Sovereign LORD says:
What sorrow awaits Jerusalem,
the city of murderers!
She is a cooking pot
whose corruption can’t be cleaned out.
Take the meat out in random order,
for no piece is better than another.
NLT.7:
For the blood of her murders
is splashed on the rocks.
It isn’t even spilled on the ground,
where the dust could cover it!
NLT.8:
So I will splash her blood on a rock
for all to see,
an expression of my anger
and vengeance against her.
NLT.9:
“This is what the Sovereign LORD says:
What sorrow awaits Jerusalem,
the city of murderers!
I myself will pile up the fuel beneath her.
NLT.10:
Yes, heap on the wood!
Let the fire roar to make the pot boil.
Cook the meat with many spices,
and afterward burn the bones.
NLT.11:
Now set the empty pot on the coals.
Heat it red hot!
Burn away the filth and corruption.
NLT.12:
But it’s hopeless;
the corruption can’t be cleaned out.
So throw it into the fire.
NLT.13:
Your impurity is your lewdness
and the corruption of your idolatry.
I tried to cleanse you,
but you refused.
So now you will remain in your filth
until my fury against you has been satisfied.
NLT.14: “I, the LORD, have spoken! The time has come, and I won’t hold back. I will not change my mind, and I will have no pity on you. You will be judged on the basis of all your wicked actions, says the Sovereign LORD.”
NLT.15: Then this message came to me from the LORD:
NLT.16: “Son of man, with one blow I will take away your dearest treasure. Yet you must not show any sorrow at her death. Do not weep; let there be no tears.
NLT.17: Groan silently, but let there be no wailing at her grave. Do not uncover your head or take off your sandals. Do not perform the usual rituals of mourning or accept any food brought to you by consoling friends.”
NLT.18: So I proclaimed this to the people the next morning, and in the evening my wife died. The next morning I did everything I had been told to do.
NLT.19: Then the people asked, “What does all this mean? What are you trying to tell us?”
NLT.20: So I said to them, “A message came to me from the LORD,
NLT.21: and I was told to give this message to the people of Israel. This is what the Sovereign LORD says: I will defile my Temple, the source of your security and pride, the place your heart delights in. Your sons and daughters whom you left behind in Judah will be slaughtered by the sword.
NLT.22: Then you will do as Ezekiel has done. You will not mourn in public or console yourselves by eating the food brought by friends.
NLT.23: Your heads will remain covered, and your sandals will not be taken off. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your sins. You will groan among yourselves for all the evil you have done.
NLT.24: Ezekiel is an example for you; you will do just as he has done. And when that time comes, you will know that I am the Sovereign LORD.”
NLT.25: Then the LORD said to me, “Son of man, on the day I take away their stronghold — their joy and glory, their heart’s desire, their dearest treasure — I will also take away their sons and daughters.
NLT.26: And on that day a survivor from Jerusalem will come to you in Babylon and tell you what has happened.
NLT.27: And when he arrives, your voice will suddenly return so you can talk to him, and you will be a symbol for these people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
